question_text: Find the derivative of tan 2x from the first principle with respect to x.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what you do with the two tangents before any limit is taken.

steps.label: State the first principle
steps.margin_note: First mark. tan 2(x + h) is tan(2x + 2h). Expand the inside angle on the same line so the next step has something to combine.

recall.must_convey: That the first principle is written with f(x) = tan 2x and the angle expanded as 2x + 2h.
accept: write the first principle for tan two x
substitute x plus h so the angle is two x plus two h
take the limit of tan two x plus two h minus tan two x over h
first principle rasi tan two x plus two h ani rasta
the derivative is the limit of the difference quotient
heard_as: tan two x plus two h

steps.why: The definition earns the mark. tan has no subtraction identity of its own, so the working has to start here and then move to sines and cosines.
common_mistakes: Quoting 2 sec²2x from the chain rule with no limit work.
steps.memory_tip: First principle first, always: f(x + h) minus f(x), all over h.

steps.label: Write it as one fraction
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two tangents can only be subtracted once they sit over one denominator. The examiner is looking for that single fraction.
lines: tan θ = sin θ/cos θ, so the numerator is

recall.must_convey: That both tangents are written as sine over cosine and combined over the common denominator cos(2x + 2h) cos 2x.
accept: write tan as sin by cos and take a common denominator
combine the two fractions over cos of two x plus two h into cos two x
cross multiply the two tangent fractions into one
tan ni sin by cos ga rasi common denominator teesukovali
put both terms over a single denominator

steps.why: There is no useful identity for tan A − tan B here. Written as sine over cosine and combined, the numerator turns into a sine of a difference, which is what removes x from the top.
common_mistakes: Using tan A − tan B = tan(A − B), which is not an identity.
Combining the numerators but leaving two separate denominators.
steps.memory_tip: For tan and cot the first move is always the same: sine over cosine, then one common denominator.

steps.label: Recognise sin 2h on top
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The whole numerator collapses to sin 2h. x has left the top, so everything that still depends on x is in the denominator.
lines: sin A cos B − cos A sin B = sin(A − B), so with

recall.must_convey: That the numerator is sin A cos B − cos A sin B = sin(A − B) and collapses to sin 2h.
accept: the numerator is sin of a minus b which is sin two h
use sin a cos b minus cos a sin b equals sin a minus b
the top becomes sin two h and the x goes away
numerator sin two h ga vasthundi
recognise the compound angle formula on top

steps.why: The numerator is exactly the expansion of sin(A − B). Recognising it removes x from the top in one line, which is what makes the limit possible at all.
common_mistakes: Reading the numerator as sin(A + B) and getting sin(4x + 2h).
Expanding the four products separately instead of matching them to the identity.
steps.memory_tip: sin A cos B − cos A sin B is sin(A − B): the sign between the terms is the sign inside the bracket.

steps.label: Take the limit
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The 2 appears because sin 2h is divided by h and not by 2h. Supplying that missing 2 is where this mark is usually lost.

recall.must_convey: That (sin 2h)/h is written as 2(sin 2h)/(2h) so the standard limit applies, giving 2 sec²2x.
accept: sin two h over h is two times sin two h over two h
the standard limit gives one so the answer is two sec squared two x
derivative of tan two x is two sec squared two x
two sec square two x answer vasthundi
multiply and divide by two to use the standard limit
heard_as: sin two h by two h

steps.why: The standard limit needs the same angle above and below. Writing (sin 2h)/h as 2(sin 2h)/(2h) supplies the missing 2, and that 2 is the derivative of the inside angle 2x.
common_mistakes: Stopping at 2/cos²2x when the answer key expects 2 sec²2x.
steps.memory_tip: sin 2h over h is 2 times sin 2h over 2h. Put the 2 in the moment you split it.
